tacit

TASS-it -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, TASS. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tacit is understood without being said.

There was a tacit understanding in the library that the corner armchair belonged to Professor Reyes.

Example

Nobody in the family ever announces it, but every Sunday at noon the kitchen fills, the big pot comes out, and everyone shows up for soup without a single reminder.

That standing Sunday plan is a tacit tradition -- understood by everyone without ever being said. Tacit describes agreements, approvals, and rules that hold full force even though no one has put them into words.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

implicit: Implicit lives inside a message: a warning implicit in a raised eyebrow, a promise implicit in a job offer. Tacit lives between people -- an agreement everyone honors without a word. A single remark can carry an implicit threat, but only a shared understanding can be tacit.

implied: Implied means someone actively hinted at a thing without saying it -- the speaker implied a deadline. It points to one sender's indirect message. Tacit needs no sender at all: both sides simply understand and honor the arrangement. A hint is implied; a silently kept bargain is tacit.

unstated: Unstated means never put into words -- an unstated assumption can sit under a plan without anyone noticing it. Tacit says more than silence: the thing is recognized, agreed to, and honored by everyone involved. An assumption may be unstated by accident; a tacit rule is obeyed on purpose.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

explicit: stated clearly and directly

declared: announced openly

Where it sits · how much silent agreement it carries — unspoken → tacit → unquestioned

unspoken vs. tacit: Unspoken is the plain, everyday label and slightly weaker than tacit -- unspoken merely reports that no one said it, while tacit adds that everyone nonetheless understands it and abides by it.

unquestioned vs. tacit: Unquestioned goes further than tacit: a tacit rule is one everyone understands and follows without saying so, while an unquestioned rule is so deeply accepted that no one even thinks to doubt it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — tac-

root — tac-: to be silent (Latin tacere)

suffix — -it

suffix — -it: past participle ending (done, made) (Latin -itus)

Put it together

Put it together: Tacit comes from Latin tacitus, 'silent' -- the past participle of tacere, 'to be silent.' A tacit agreement is literally a silent one: nothing was said out loud, yet everyone understood.

Use the root in a new word: taciturn

Use the root in a new word: taciturn: Our taciturn neighbor waves hello every morning but rarely says more than two words.

Root Check

Word Choice

Tacit attaches to agreements, approval, consent, and understandings: tacit approval, tacit consent, a tacit understanding. It marks things agreed to in silence -- if someone nods along without objecting, their approval is tacit. Its opposite is explicit: stated outright, in so many words.
